text:
Ellen Park: Heads-up: planning session for 'Optimize Advisor' roadmap slice. Goal: ship an opinionated MVP that helps customers reduce token spend without regressing quality. Need final scope decisions by EOD Fri. @Diego @Tara

Diego Ramirez: Propose MVP pillars: 1) route-level batching recs, 2) KV caching TTLs with hit-rate estimates, 3) eval-triggered alerts integrated with Slack (no PD at first). Keep quantization doc-only.

Tara Singh: Strong +1. Add acceptance criteria: recommender exposes confidence score, show expected cost % delta, and a quick rollback recipe if eval drops. The UI can be a simple table + "Export JSON" button.

Noah Li: From infra side: need to lock data windows for telemetry (7d rolling) and a lightweight simulator to estimate latency/cost. Otherwise recommendations will be noisy. Also recommend a canary path: apply recs to <5% traffic via routing policy.

Ellen Park: Good. For pilot customers we should aim for 2 verticals: conversational chat (low latency) and long-form generation (high tokens). Lina flagged AcmeHealth earlier; any other warm leads?

Diego Ramirez: GammaLabs is interested in batch summarization. I'll confirm. For canary we should support route tags and per-route SLOs so we can measure p95 change.

Tara Singh: UX: show "quality delta estimate" from evals. We can run paired-eval on historical prompts to estimate. If the delta > 1% (absolute) we mark as 'needs human review'.

Noah Li: Implementation notes: recommender will ingest per-request payload size, latency, and cost. Output schema (example): ```json
{"route":"/v1/generate","rec_type":"batching","confidence":0.82,"expected_cost_change":"-18%","expected_p95_ms":+30}
``` Keep schema minimal.

Ellen Park: Workflow decision: MVP supports "suggest and export" only. Auto-apply and automated quantization deferred to next quarter. Pilot gating: 1) two pilots onboarded, 2) <1% observed quality regression across pilot datasets, 3) docs and SDK snippet exportable.

Diego Ramirez: Timeline: POC recommender + simulator (2 sprints), export + SDK glue (0.5 sprint), eval hooking + Slack alerts (0.5 sprint). We can parallelize SDK and alerts.

Tara Singh: Pilot acceptance testcases: short conversational prompt set (50 queries), long-form prompt set (20 docs), and an adversarial set to stress quality. We'll define pass/fail thresholds.

pilot-bot: Created card OPT-2983 in Projects. Subtasks: recommender-poc, simulator, sdk-export, eval-alerts, pilot-runbooks. https://projects.internal/OPT-2983 :spiral_calendar:

Ellen Park: Risk log note: batching increases tail latency; need to quantify p99 impact and include a hard SLO check before recommending. Also add "explainability" field so engineers know why a rec was suggested.

Noah Li: Suggest we include a lightweight cost model per GPU type so we can convert token savings to $ estimates. That will help PMs & customers evaluate ROI.

Diego Ramirez: Agreed. We'll add a dollar estimate column in the export. Also plan a short design doc with sample API responses and ranking formula by EOD Tue.

Tara Singh: I'll draft pilot onboarding email and a quickstart with two config snippets: one for low-latency chat and one for high-throughput batch. Example quickstart snippet: ```json
{"route":"/v1/chat","batching":{"enabled":true,"target_latency_ms":150},"cache":{"prefix":"session:","ttl_seconds":30}}
```

Ellen Park: Great. If no objections I'll lock scope to "suggest+export, eval-alert slack only, docs+2 pilots". We will revisit auto-apply and quantization automation in next planning cycle. Thanks team :thumbsup:
